<h1 id="rocket-services">Rocket Services v3.730.300-ref-1-39-0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

An Orchestration Layer that takes ISL services and packages them in a more targeted way for front-end applications.
This in turn makes client integration easier and reduces the complexity and size of front-end applications.

Rocket is also customisable - allowing UI engineers to ‘remix’ the existing back-end services into something that
best suits the application they are developing.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.apis.guru/api">https://api.apis.guru/api</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. Account JWT token

    - Flow: password
    - Token URL = [/account/authorization](/account/authorization)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|Catalog|Access all read only content|
|Commerce|Perform account level transactions|
|Playback|Allow playback of restricted content|
|Settings|Modify account settings|

- oAuth2 authentication. Profile JWT token

    - Flow: password
    - Token URL = [/account/profile/authorization](/account/profile/authorization)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|Catalog|Modify profile preferences and activity (bookmarks, watch list)|

* API Key (resetPasswordAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **authorization**, in: header.

* API Key (verifyEmailAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **authorization**, in: header.

<h1 id="rocket-services-account">account</h1>

## getAccount

<a id="opIdgetAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account`

Get the details of an account along with the profiles and entitlements under it.

<h3 id="getaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## updateAccount

<a id="opIdupdateAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": {
      "addressLine1": "string",
      "addressLine2": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postcode": "string",
      "state": "string"
    },
    "defaultPaymentInstrumentId": "string",
    "defaultPaymentMethodId": "string",
    "firstName": "string",
    "lastName": "string",
    "minRatingPlaybackGuard": "string",
    "segments": [
      "string"
    ],
    "trackingEnabled": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /account`

Update the details of an account.

With the exception of the address, this supports partial updates, so you can send just the
properties you wish to update.

When the address is provided any properties which are omitted from the address will be cleared.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": {
    "addressLine1": "string",
    "addressLine2": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "postcode": "string",
    "state": "string"
  },
  "defaultPaymentInstrumentId": "string",
  "defaultPaymentMethodId": "string",
  "firstName": "string",
  "lastName": "string",
  "minRatingPlaybackGuard": "string",
  "segments": [
    "string"
  ],
  "trackingEnabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="updateaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[AccountUpdateRequest](#schemaaccountupdaterequest)|true|Updated account details.|
|» address|body|[Address](#schemaaddress)|false|none|
|» defaultPaymentInstrumentId|body|string|false|The id of the payment instrument to use by default for account transactions.<br><br>**DEPRECATED** The property `defaultPaymentMethodId` is now preferred.<br>|
|» defaultPaymentMethodId|body|string|false|The id of the payment method to use by default for account transactions.|
|» firstName|body|string|false|The first name of the account holder.|
|» lastName|body|string|false|The last name of the account holder.|
|» minRatingPlaybackGuard|body|string|false|The classification rating defining the minimum rating level a user should be<br>forced to enter the account pin code for playback. Anything at this rating<br>level or above will require the pin for playback.<br><br>e.g. AUOFLC-MA15+<br><br>If you want to disable this guard pass an empty string or `null`.<br>|
|» segments|body|[string]|false|The segments an account should be placed under|
|» trackingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether usage tracking is associated with an account or anonymous.|

## addPaymentMethod

<a id="opIdaddPaymentMethod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/billing/methods \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "makeDefault": true,
    "token": "string",
    "type": "Card"
  }'
```

`POST /account/billing/methods`

Add a new payment method to an account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "makeDefault": true,
  "token": "string",
  "type": "Card"
}
```

<h3 id="addpaymentmethod-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[AddPaymentMethodRequest](#schemaaddpaymentmethodrequest)|true|Registration details for a new payment method.|
|» makeDefault|body|boolean|false|Whether this payment method should become the account default when <br>making purchases.<br><br>Note that if this is the first payment method of type Card being added to an<br>account then it will become the default whether this property is true or false.<br>|

## makePurchase

<a id="opIdmakePurchase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/billing/purchases \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "paymentMethodId": "string",
    "planId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /account/billing/purchases`

Purchase a plan or item offer.
The result of a successful transaction is a new entitlement.


> Body parameter

```json

  "itemId": "string",
  "offerId": "string",
  "paymentMethodId": "string",
  "planId": "string"
}
```

## authorizeDevice

<a id="opIdauthorizeDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/devices/authorization \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /account/devices/authorization`

Authorize a device from a generated device authorization code.

This is the second step in the process of authorizing a device by pin code.

Firstly the device must request a generated authorization code via the
`/authorization/device/code` endpoint.

This endpoint then authorizes the device associated with the code to sign in
to a user account. Typically this endpoint will be called from a page
presented in the web app under the account section.

Once authorized, the device will then be able to sign in to that account
via the `/authorization/device` endpoint, without needing to provide the 
credentials of the user.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="authorizedevice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[DeviceAuthorizationCode](#schemadeviceauthorizationcode)|true|The generated device authorization code.|
|» code|body|string|true|The generated device authorization code.|

## getItemMediaFiles

<a id="opIdgetItemMediaFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/account/items/string/videos?delivery=stream&resolution=HD-4K' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/items/{id}/videos`

Get the video files associated with an item given maximum resolution, device type
and one or more delivery types.

This endpoint accepts an Account Catalog token, however if when requesting
playback files you receive an *403 status code with error code 1* then the file
you're requesting is classification restricted. This means you should switch
to target the `/account/items/{id}/videos-guarded` endpoint, passing it an Account
Playback token. If not already obtained, this token can be requested via the
`/itv/pinauthorization` endpoint with an account level pin.

For convenience you may also access free / public files through this endpoint
instead of the /items/{id}/videos endpoint, when authenticated.

Returns an array of video file objects which each include a url to a video.

The first entry in the array contains what is predicted to be the best match.
The remainder of the entries, if any, may contain resolutions below what was
requests. For example if you request HD-720 the response may also contain
SD entries.

If you specify multiple delivery types, then the response array will insert
types in the order you specify them in the query. For example `stream,progressive`
would return an array with 0 or more stream files followed by 0 or more progressive files.

If no files are found a 404 is returned.


<h3 id="getitemmediafiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The identifier of the item whose video files to load.|
|delivery|query|[string]|true|The video delivery type you require.|
|resolution|query|string|true|The maximum resolution the device to playback the media can present.|
|formats|query|[string]|false|The set of media file formats that the device supports, in the order of preference.<br><br>When provided, Rocket API returns only media files in formats specified in this parameter. For each resolution, only the first media file of matching supported format is returned. Files of different resolutions may be of different supported media file formats.<br><br>`external` value is reserved for project customizations where the real MIME type of the file on the specified URL is unknown at the time of ingestion.<br><br>When not provided, Rocket API uses the legacy `User-Agent` header-based logic to find matching media files.<br>|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|

## getItemMediaFilesGuarded

<a id="opIdgetItemMediaFilesGuarded"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/account/items/string/videos-guarded?delivery=stream&resolution=HD-4K' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/items/{id}/videos-guarded`

Get the video files associated with an item given maximum resolution, device type
and one or more delivery types.

This endpoint is identical to the `/account/items/{id}/videos` however it expects
an Account Playback token. This token, and in association this endpoint, is specifically
for use when playback files are classification restricted and require an account
level pin to access them.

Returns an array of video file objects which each include a url to a video.

The first entry in the array contains what is predicted to be the best match.
The remainder of the entries, if any, may contain resolutions below what was
requests. For example if you request HD-720 the response may also contain
SD entries.

If you specify multiple delivery types, then the response array will insert
types in the order you specify them in the query. For example `stream,progressive`
would return an array with 0 or more stream files followed by 0 or more progressive files.

If no files are found a 404 is returned.

## generateNonce

<a id="opIdgenerateNonce"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/nonce \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/nonce`

Generate a new account nonce.

A nonce may be required to help sign a response from a third party
service which will be passed back to these services.

For example a Facebook single-sign-on request initiated by a client
application may first get a nonce from here to include in the request.
Facebook will then include the nonce in the auth token it issues. This
token can be passed back to our services and the nonce checked for validity.

Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|

## requestEmailVerification

<a id="opIdrequestEmailVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/request-email-verification \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /account/request-email-verification`

Request that the email address tied to an account be verified.

This will send a verification email to the email address of the primary profile containing
a link which, once clicked, completes the verification process via the /verify-email endpoint.

Note that when an account is created this email is sent automatically so there's no need
to call this directly.

If the user doesn't click the link before it expires then this endpoint can be called
to request a new verification email. In the future it may also be used if we add support
for changing an account email address.


<h3 id="requestemailverification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. ## getBookmarks

<a id="opIdgetBookmarks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/bookmarks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/bookmarks`

Get the map of bookmarked item ids (itemId => creationDate) under the active profile.

<h3 id="getbookmarks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## getContinueWatchingList

<a id="opIdgetContinueWatchingList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/continue-watching/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/continue-watching/list`

Returns a list of items which have been watched but not completed under the active
profile.

Multiple episodes under the same show may be watched or in progress, however only a
single item belonging to a particular show will be included in the returned list.

The next episode to continue watching for a particular show will be the most recent
incompletely watched episode, or the next episode following the most recently
completely watched episode. Based on the specified `show_item_type` type, either the next
episode, the season of the next episode, or the show will be included in the list.


<h3 id="getcontinuewatchinglist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|show_item_type|query|string|false|The item type to be returned for continue watching items belonging to a show.<br><br>Multiple episodes under the same show may be watched or in progress, however only a<br>single item belonging to a particular show will be included in the returned list.<br><br>The next episode to continue watching for a particular show will be the most recent<br>incompletely watched episode, or the next episode following the most recently<br>completely watched episode. Based on the specified `show_item_type` type, either the next<br>episode, the season of the next episode, or the show will be included in the list.<br><br>If `episode` is specified, then only the next episode to continue watching for a<br>show will be returned.<br><br>If `season` is specified, then only the season of the next episode will be returned.<br><br>If `show` is specified, then only the show of the next episode will be returned<br><br>The recommended value of this parameter should reflect the desitination the<br>user will be sent to when they select this item in the list. So if a user will<br>be sent to the show detail page then this should be `show` and you can use<br>the `include` parameter to get metadata about the episode or season if needed<br>|
|include|query|[string]|false|Include one opr more ancestor/children for items belonging to a show. Extra items<br>will be populated in the `listData` property of the list<br><br>If no value is specified no dependencies are included.<br><br>If `episode` is specified, then the next episode will be added for season/show<br>items. Has no effect if `show_item_type` is set to `episode`.<br><br>If `season` is specified, then the season of the next episode will be added for<br>episode/show items. Has no effect if `show_item_type` is set to `season`.<br><br>If `show` is specified, then the show of the next episode will be added for<br>episode/season items. Has no effect if `show_item_type` is set to `show`.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page of items to load. Starts from page 1.|
|page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to return in a page.|
|max_rating|query|string|false|The maximum rating (inclusive) of an item returned, e.g. 'auoflc-pg'.|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

|include|season|
|include|show|

<aside class="warning">

profileAuth ( Scopes: Catalog )
</aside>

## getNextPlaybackItem

<a id="opIdgetNextPlaybackItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/items/string/next \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/items/{itemId}/next`

Returns the next item to play given a source item id.

For an unwatched show it returns the first episode available to the account.

For a watched show it returns the last incompletely watched episode by the profile,
or the episode that immediately follows the last completely watched episode 
or nothing.

For an episode it always returns the immediately following episode, if available to
the account, or nothing.

If the response does not contain a `next` property then no item was found.


<h3 id="getnextplaybackitem-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemId|path|string|true|The identifier of the source item to base the next to watch item off.<br>|
|max_rating|query|string|false|The maximum rating (inclusive) of an item returned, e.g. 'auoflc-pg'.|
|expand|query|string|false|If no value is specified no dependencies are expanded.<br><br>If 'parent' is specified then only the direct parent will be expanded.<br>For example if an `Episode` then the `Season` would be included.<br><br>If 'ancestors' is specified then the full parent chain is expanded.<br>For example if an `Episode` then both the `Season` and `Show` would be included.<br>|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|parent|
|expand|ancestors|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|

## getRatings

<a id="opIdgetRatings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/ratings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/ratings`

Get the map of rated item ids (itemId => rating out of 10) under the active profile.

<h3 id="getratings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|

## getRatingsList

<a id="opIdgetRatingsList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/ratings/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/ratings/list`

Returns the list of rated items under the active profile.

<h3 id="getratingslist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page of items to load. Starts from page 1.|
|page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to return in a page.|
|order|query|string|false|The list sort order, either 'asc' or 'desc'.|
|order_by|query|string|false|What to order by.<br><br>Ordering by `date-modified` equates to ordering by the last rated date.<br>|
|item_type|query|string|false|The item type to filter by. Defaults to unspecified.|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## getItemWatchedStatus

<a id="opIdgetItemWatchedStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/profile/watched/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /account/profile/watched/{itemId}`

Get the watched status info for an item under the active profile.

<h3 id="getitemwatchedstatus-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemId|path|string|true|The id of the item to get the watched status for.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

{
  "firstWatchedDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "isFullyWatched": false,
  "itemId": "string",
  "lastWatchedDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "position": 0
}

## setItemWatchedStatus

<a id="opIdsetItemWatchedStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/account/profile/watched/string?position=0' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /account/profile/watched/{itemId}`

Record the watched playhead position of a video under the active profile.

Can be used later to resume a video from where it was last watched.

Creates one if it doesn't exist, overwrites one if it does.


<h3 id="setitemwatchedstatus-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemId|path|string|true|The id of the item being watched.|
|position|query|integer(int32)|true|The playhead position to record.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|

  "firstWatchedDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "isFullyWatched": false,

  "position": 0

## getAccountToken

<a id="opIdgetAccountToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/authorization \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "",
    "password": "",
    "scopes": [
      "Catalog"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /authorization`

Request one or more `Account` level authorization tokens each with a chosen scope.

Tokens are used to access restricted service endpoints. These restricted endpoints
will require a specific token type (e.g Account) with a specific scope (e.g. Catalog)
before access is granted.

For convenience, where a Profile level token with the same scope exists it will also be returned.

Authorization with pin is not supported on this endpoint anymore. Use `/itv/pinauthorization`
endpoint instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "",
  "password": "",
  "scopes": [
    "Catalog"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="getaccounttoken-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[AccountTokenRequest](#schemaaccounttokenrequest)|true|The account credentials with requested token scope.|

This is only intended for web based clients which<br>need to pass the cookies to a server to render a page based on the user's<br>content filters e.g subscription code.<br><br>If type `Session` the cookie will be session based.<br>If type `Persistent` the cookie will have a medium term lifespan.<br>If undefined no cookies will be set.<br>|
|» email|body|string|true|The email associated with the account.|
|» password|body|string|true|The password associated with the account.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|true|The scope(s) of the tokens required.<br>For each scope listed an Account and Profile token of that scope will be returned<br>|

## getAccountTokenByCode

<a id="opIdgetAccountTokenByCode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/authorization/device \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "code": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "scopes": [
      "Catalog"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /authorization/device`

Get Catalog tokens for an account using a device authorization code.
Where a Profile level token of Catalog scope exists it will also be returned.

This is the final step in the process of authorizing a device by pin code.

Firstly the device must request a generated authorization code via the
`/authorization/device/code` endpoint.

The code is subsequently used to authorize the device to sign in to a given
account via the `/account/devices/authorization` endpoint. Typically this
will be from a page presented in the web app under the account section.

Once authorized, this endpoint will allow the device to sign in without
needing to provide the credentials of the user.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "scopes": [
    "Catalog"
  ]
}
```

|body|body|[AccountTokenByCodeRequest](#schemaaccounttokenbycoderequest)|true|The device id e.g. serial number and authorization code.|
|» code|body|string|true|The generated device authorization code.|
|» id|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the device e.g. serial number.|

## generateDeviceAuthorizationCode

<a id="opIdgenerateDeviceAuthorizationCode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/authorization/device/code \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /authorization/device/code`

Get a generated device authorization code.

This is the first step in the process of authorizing a device by pin code.
The device will make a request to this endpoint providing a unique identifier
for the device such as a serial number. This endpoint will then return a
generated code which is tied to the given device.

The code may subsequently be used to authorize the device to sign in to an
account via the `/account/devices/authorization` endpoint. Typically this
will be from a page presented in the web app under the account section.

Once authorized, the device will then be able to sign in to that account
via the `/authorization/device` endpoint, without needing to provide the 
credentials of the user.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="generatedeviceauthorizationcode-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[DeviceRegistrationRequest](#schemadeviceregistrationrequest)|true|Details of the device being authorized.|
|» id|body|string|true|The unique identifier for this device e.g. serial number.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human recognisable name for this device.|
|» type|body|string|true|The device type e.g. web_browser.|

## singleSignOn

<a id="opIdsingleSignOn"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/authorization/sso \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "cookieType": "Session",
    "linkAccounts": true,
    "provider": "Facebook",
    "scopes": [
      "Catalog"
    ],
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /authorization/sso`

Exchange a third party single-sign-on token for our own authorization tokens.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cookieType": "Session",
  "linkAccounts": true,
  "provider": "Facebook",
  "scopes": [
    "Catalog"
  ],
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="singlesignon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[SingleSignOnRequest](#schemasinglesignonrequest)|true|A single-sign-on request.|
|» cookieType|body|string|false|If you specify a cookie type then a content filter cookie will be returned<br>along with the token(s). This is only intended for web based clients which<br>need to pass the cookies to a server to render a page based on the user's<br>content filters e.g subscription code.<br><br>If type `Session` the cookie will be session based.<br>If type `Persistent` the cookie will have a medium term lifespan.<br>If undefined no cookies will be set.<br>|
|» linkAccounts|body|boolean|false|When a user attempts to sign in using single-sign-on, we may find an account created<br>previously through the manual sign up flow with the same email. ## forgotPassword

<a id="opIdforgotPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/request-password-reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /request-password-reset`

Request the password of an account's primary profile be reset.

Should be called when a user has forgotten their password.

This will send an email with a password reset link to the email address of the
primary profile of an account.

The link, once clicked, should take the user to the "reset-password" page of the
website. Here they will enter their new password and submit to the /reset-password
endpoint here, along with the password reset token provided in the original link.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="forgotpassword-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[PasswordResetEmailRequest](#schemapasswordresetemailrequest)|true|Email address of account to request a password reset on.|
|» email|body|string|true|The email address of the primary account profile to reset the password for.|

## resetPassword

<a id="opIdresetPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/reset-password \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "password": "string",
    "resetToken": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /reset-password`

When a user requests to reset their password via the /request-password-reset endpoint, an
email is sent to the email address of the primary profile of the account. This email contains a link
with a reset token as query parameter. The link should take the user to the "reset-password"
page of the website.

From the reset-password page a user should enter the new password they wish to use. 
It should then be submitted to this endpoint,
along with the reset token from the email link. 
The token should be provided in the body as resetToken property.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "string",
  "resetToken": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="resetpassword-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[PasswordResetRequest](#schemapasswordresetrequest)|true|ITV reset token from email link and a new password.|
|» password|body|string|true|The new password for the account.|
|» resetToken|body|string|true|The ITV reset token.|

## verifyEmail

<a id="opIdverifyEmail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/verify-email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /verify-email`

When an account is created an email is sent to the email address of the new account.
This contains a link, which once clicked, verifies the email address of the account is correct.

The link contains a token as a query parameter which should be passed as the authorization
bearer token to this endpoint to complete email verification.

The token has en expiry, so if the link is not clicked before it expires, the account holder
may need to request a new verification email be sent. This can be done via the endpoint
/account/request-email-verification.


<h3 id="verifyemail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

## getAppConfig

<a id="opIdgetAppConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /config`

Get the global configuration for an application. Should be called during app statup.

This includes things like device and playback rules, classifications,
sitemap and subscriptions.

You have the option to select specific configuration objects using the 'include'
parameter, or if unspecified, getting all configuration.


<h3 id="getappconfig-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[string]|false|A comma delimited list of config objects to return.<br>If none specified then all configuration is returned.<br>|
|system|query|string|false|Classification system to load in case include = classification.<br>|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## getItvPage

<a id="opIdgetItvPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/itv/page?path=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /itv/page`

Returns a page with the specified id.

This is a cut down version for low memory devices.123

If targeting the search page you must url encode the search term as a parameter
using the `q` key. For example if your browser path looks like `/search?q=the`
then what you pass to this endpoint would look like `/itv/page?path=/search%3Fq%3Dthe`.


<h3 id="getitvpage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|query|string|true|The path of the page to load, e.g. '/movies'.|
|list_page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to load when prefetching and paging each list in the page row.|
|list_page_size_large|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to load when prefetching a continuous scroll list entry in a page.<br><br>By default any list page entry with template pattern `/^CS\d+$/` will<br>be considered a continuous scroll list.<br>|
|max_list_prefetch|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of lists to prefetch in the page.|
|item_detail_expand|query|string|false|Only relevant when loading item detail pages as these embed a detailed item in the main page entry.<br><br>If no value is specified no item dependencies are expanded.<br><br>If 'children' is specified then the list of any direct children will be expanded. For example<br>seasons of a show or episodes of a season.<br><br>If 'all' is specified then the parent chain will be expanded along with any child list at each level.<br>For example if an episode is specified then its season will be expanded and that season's episode list.<br>The season will have its show expanded and the show will have its season list expanded.<br><br>The 'all' options is useful when you deep link into a show/season/episode for the first time as<br>it provides full context for navigating around the show page. Subsequent navigation around<br>children of the show should only need to request expand of children.<br><br>If 'ancestors' is specified then only the parent chain is included<br><br>If an expand is specified which is not relevant to the item type, it will be ignored.<br>|
|item_detail_select_season|query|string|false|Only relevant when loading show detail pages as these embed a detailed item in the main page entry.<br><br>Since the introduction of the D1,2,3 templates this parameter is now somewhat redundant, or less<br>likely to have any effect. While it may still be useful in some cases, most of the time the season<br>selection will be dictated by the configuration of the rows scheduled on the show detail page.<br>This parameter will only take effect if there are rows used to schedule episodes of a season, like<br>D1,2,3, or if no rows have a value set for their `seasonOrder` custom field.<br><br>Given a targeted show page, it can be useful to get the details of a child season. This option<br>provides a means to return the `first` or `latest` season of a show embedded in the page.<br><br>The `expand` parameter also works here so for example you could land on a show page and request the<br>`item_detail_select_season=latest` along with `item_detail_expand=all`. This would then return the<br>detail of the latest season with its list of child episode summaries, and also expand<br>the detail of the show with its list of seasons summaries.<br>|
|text_entry_format|query|string|false|Only relevant to page entries of type `TextEntry`.<br><br>Converts the value of a text page entry to the specified format.<br>|
|max_rating|query|string|false|The maximum rating (inclusive) of items returned, e.g. 'auoflc-pg'.|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|item_detail_expand|all|
|item_detail_expand|children|
|item_detail_expand|ancestors|
|item_detail_select_season|first|
|item_detail_select_season|latest|
|text_entry_format|markdown|
|text_entry_format|html|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|

<h3 id="getitvpage-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The page requested.|[Page](#schemapage)|
|301|Moved Permanently|Returned if feature flag `cd` is set and item detail is requested of an item that has<br>Custom Destination set to an External URL. The `Location` response header contains the URL.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|[ServiceError](#schemaserviceerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not found.|[ServiceError](#schemaserviceerror)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|[ServiceError](#schemaserviceerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|[ServiceError](#schemaserviceerror)|
|default|Default|Service error.|[ServiceError](#schemaserviceerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## getPage

<a id="opIdgetPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/page?path=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /page`

Returns a page with the specified id.

If targeting the search page you must url encode the search term as a parameter
using the `q` key. For example if your browser path looks like `/search?q=the`
then what you pass to this endpoint would look like `/page?path=/search%3Fq%3Dthe`.


<h3 id="getpage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|path|query|string|true|The path of the page to load, e.g. '/movies'.|
|list_page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to load when prefetching and paging each list in the page row.|
|list_page_size_large|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to load when prefetching a continuous scroll list entry in a page.<br><br>By default any list page entry with template pattern `/^CS\d+$/` will<br>be considered a continuous scroll list.<br>|
|max_list_prefetch|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of lists to prefetch in the page.|
|item_detail_expand|query|string|false|Only relevant when loading item detail pages as these embed a detailed item in the main page entry.<br><br>If no value is specified no item dependencies are expanded.<br><br>If 'children' is specified then the list of any direct children will be expanded. For example<br>seasons of a show or episodes of a season.<br><br>If 'all' is specified then the parent chain will be expanded along with any child list at each level.<br>For example if an episode is specified then its season will be expanded and that season's episode list.<br>The season will have its show expanded and the show will have its season list expanded.<br><br>The 'all' options is useful when you deep link into a show/season/episode for the first time as<br>it provides full context for navigating around the show page. Subsequent navigation around<br>children of the show should only need to request expand of children.<br><br>If 'ancestors' is specified then only the parent chain is included<br><br>If an expand is specified which is not relevant to the item type, it will be ignored.<br>|
|item_detail_select_season|query|string|false|Only relevant when loading show detail pages as these embed a detailed item in the main page entry.<br><br>Since the introduction of the D1,2,3 templates this parameter is now somewhat redundant, or less<br>likely to have any effect. While it may still be useful in some cases, most of the time the season<br>selection will be dictated by the configuration of the rows scheduled on the show detail page.<br>This parameter will only take effect if there are rows used to schedule episodes of a season, like<br>D1,2,3, or if no rows have a value set for their `seasonOrder` custom field.<br><br>Given a targeted show page, it can be useful to get the details of a child season. This option<br>provides a means to return the `first` or `latest` season of a show embedded in the page.<br><br>The `expand` parameter also works here so for example you could land on a show page and request the<br>`item_detail_select_season=latest` along with `item_detail_expand=all`. This would then return the<br>detail of the latest season with its list of child episode summaries, and also expand<br>the detail of the show with its list of seasons summaries.<br>|
|text_entry_format|query|string|false|Only relevant to page entries of type `TextEntry`.<br><br>Converts the value of a text page entry to the specified format.<br>|
|max_rating|query|string|false|The maximum rating (inclusive) of items returned, e.g. 'auoflc-pg'.|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## checkEeBtEligibility

<a id="opIdcheckEeBtEligibility"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/ee-bt/eligibility \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ee-bt/eligibility`

Check whether or not a user is eligible for switching to Bt or EE offers.

<h3 id="checkeebteligibility-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "eligible": true,
  "plan": "string",
  "source": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="checkeebteligibility-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success, returns eligibility data.|[EeBtEligibility](#schemaeebteligibility)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Customer does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
accountAuth ( Scopes: Catalog )
</aside>

## getEligibleOffers

<a id="opIdgetEligibleOffers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/ee/offers \

  -d '{
    "accessToken": "wxg0fG4GQjBQVjAT0AhKxSkrxFbs",

    "trackingHeader": "1234E682-2C74-46A4-B8B3-5BBD3B3E165D"
  }'
```

`POST /ee/offers`

Returns eligible partner specific offers for the querying partner for an EE MSISDN.
This call is supposed to be called after we have MSISDN accired.
This call should be followed by POST /ee/msisdn.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accessToken": "wxg0fG4GQjBQVjAT0AhKxSkrxFbs",
  "msisdn": "447931234567",
  "trackingHeader": "1234E682-2C74-46A4-B8B3-5BBD3B3E165D"
}
```

<h3 id="geteligibleoffers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|
|body|body|[EeOffersRequest](#schemaeeoffersrequest)|true|Data for getting the eligible offers.|
|» accessToken|body|string|true|EE API authorization Token received from GET /ee/token/create.|
|» msisdn|body|string|true|The msisdn.|
|» trackingHeader|body|string|false|trackingHeader.|

|id|path|string|true|The identifier of the plan received from ee/offers.|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

## createToken

<a id="opIdcreateToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/ee/token/create \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /ee/token/create`

Returns a token for later calls to EE API. TTL is one hour. Recommended is FE refreshes this token before each call.

> Example responses

<h1 id="rocket-services-content">content</h1>

## getItem

<a id="opIdgetItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/items/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /items/{id}`

Returns the details of an item with the specified id.

<h3 id="getitem-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The identifier of the item to load.<br><br>The custom identifier of an item can be used here if the `use_custom_id` parameter is true.<br>|
|max_rating|query|string|false|The maximum rating (inclusive) of items returned, e.g. 'auoflc-pg'.|
|expand|query|string|false|If no value is specified no dependencies are expanded.<br><br>If 'children' is specified then the list of any direct children will be expanded. For example<br>seasons of a show or episodes of a season.<br><br>If 'all' is specified then the parent chain will be expanded along with any child list at each level.<br>For example if an episode is specified then its season will be expanded and that season's episode list.<br>The season will have its show expanded and the show will have its season list expanded.<br><br>The 'all' options is useful when you deep link into a show/season/episode for the first time as<br>it provides full context for navigating around the show page. Subsequent navigation around<br>children of the show should only need to request expand of children.<br><br>If 'ancestors' is specified then only the parent chain is included.<br><br>If 'parent' is specified then only the direct parent is included.<br><br>If an expand is specified which is not relevant to the item type, it will be ignored.<br>|
|select_season|query|string|false|Given a provided show id, it can be useful to get the details of a child season. This option<br>provides a means to return the `first` or `latest` season of a show given the show id.<br><br>The `expand` parameter also works here so for example you could land on a show page and request the<br>latest season along with `expand=all`. This would then return the detail of the latest season with<br>its list of child episode summaries, and also expand the detail of the show with its list of seasons summaries.<br><br>Note the `id` parameter must be a show id for this parameter to work correctly.<br>|
|use_custom_id|query|boolean|false|Set to true when passing a custom Id as the `id` path parameter.|
|device|query|string|false|The type of device the content is targeting.|
|sub|query|string|false|The active subscription code.|
|segments|query|[string]|false|The list of segments to filter the response by.|
|ff|query|[string]|false|The set of opt in feature flags which cause breaking changes to responses.<br><br>While Rocket APIs look to avoid breaking changes under the active major version, the formats of responses<br>may need to evolve over this time.<br><br>These feature flags allow clients to select which response formats they expect and avoid breaking<br>clients as these formats evolve under the current major version.<br><br>### Flags<br><br>- `all` - Enable all flags. Useful for testing. _Don't use in production_.<br>- `idp` - Dynamic item detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `ldp` - Dynamic list detail pages with schedulable rows.<br>- `hb` - Hubble formatted image urls.<br>- `rpt` - Updated resume point threshold logic.<br>- `cas` - "Custom Asset Search", inlcude `customAssets` in search results.<br>- `lrl` - Do not pre-populate related list if more than `max_list_prefetch` down the page.<br>- `cd` - Custom Destination support.<br><br>See the `feature-flags.md` for available flag details.<br>|
|lang|query|string|false|Language code for the preferred language to be returned in the response.<br><br>Parameter value is case-insensitive and should be<br>  - a valid 2 letter language code without region such as en, de<br>  - or with region such as en_us, en_au<br><br>If undefined then defaults to 'en', unless the server has been configured<br>with a custom default.<br><br>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|all|
|expand|children|
|expand|ancestors|
|expand|parent|
|select_season|first|
|select_season|latest|
|ff|all|
|ff|idp|
|ff|ldp|
|ff|hb|
|ff|rpt|
|ff|cas|
|ff|lrl|
|ff|cd|
